definition: A network interface with a private IP in one of your subnets that leads to one specific Azure resource, such as a database server or a storage account's blob service, over Private Link. It does not close the resource's public endpoint by itself - you disable public network access separately. About $7 a month each plus data.
example: pe-sql-orders gives the orders database the address 10.20.2.4 in snet-pe, and public network access on the server is disabled.

definition: The Azure technology behind private endpoints: it carries traffic from a private IP in your VNet to a specific resource entirely over Microsoft's network. A Private Link service lets you publish your own application to other VNets or customers the same way.
example: Front Door Premium reaches the API origin over Private Link, so the App Service needs no public endpoint.

definition: A free subnet setting that sends traffic for an Azure service over Microsoft's backbone and lets that service's firewall trust the subnet. The resource keeps using its public address, it cannot be reached from on-premises this way, and it applies to the whole service rather than one resource. Private endpoints have largely replaced it for data.
example: A service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage lets snet-vm reach storage without a private endpoint, but the account's public address stays in use.

definition: A DNS zone that only answers inside the VNets linked to it. For private endpoints it holds the privatelink name of each resource, such as privatelink.database.windows.net, so the unchanged public name resolves to the private IP inside your network. Create one per service type, once, and link it to every VNet.
example: privatelink.database.windows.net lives in the hub and is linked to hub, prod and dev, so sql-shop-prod resolves to 10.20.2.4 everywhere.

definition: A managed DNS service with inbound and outbound endpoints on ordinary private IPs, so on-premises DNS servers can forward Azure private names into Azure, and Azure can forward on-premises names out. Replaces home-built DNS forwarder VMs. Roughly $180 a month per endpoint.
example: The office DNS server forwards every privatelink name to the resolver's inbound endpoint at 10.0.2.4 in the hub.

definition: Connects networks to Azure over encrypted IPsec tunnels across the internet: site-to-site joins an office router to a VNet, point-to-site gives individual laptops a VPN client with Entra ID sign-in. It sits in a subnet called GatewaySubnet, starts around $140 a month, and is only as steady as the internet line under it.
example: A site-to-site VPN joins the office's 192.168.0.0/16 to the hub; ExpressRoute is kept for when bandwidth demands it.

definition: A private circuit between your premises or data centre and Microsoft, bought through a connectivity provider, that never crosses the internet. It gives predictable latency and bandwidth from 50 Mbps to 10 Gbps and more, with a 99.95% SLA, but costs far more than a VPN, takes weeks to provision, and is not encrypted unless you add MACsec or a VPN on top.
example: A bank replicating databases to Azure uses ExpressRoute, with a site-to-site VPN as its backup path.
